title: Queued warmup safeguard and routing adjustments to stabilize TTFT/tokens/sec across deployments
creator: Maya Rodriguez
description: High-severity customer escalations observed across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments: intermittent TTFT regressions and a 20-40% tokens/sec drop for mixed short/long context workloads. Investigation shows a common causal chain: concurrent KV-cache warmup spikes plus an aggressive kernel-selection preemption path that drops multiplex throughput under heavy small-request fanout. This ticket implements a short-term safeguard: a queued warmup admission controller + priority-aware routing adjustments to prevent warmup storms, plus a targeted kernel-selection throttling heuristic rollback. The goal is to stop customer impact within the SLA window and provide deterministic canary rollouts to Dedicated customers before full deploy to Hosted and Private images.
notes: 2026-03-10 02:12 UTC: Pager alert from monitoring (TTFT p95 crossing SLA) triggered. Initial spike correlated with KV-cache miss rate increasing by 7x for short requests.

2026-03-10 02:45 UTC: Reproduced locally using mixed-shard replay workload (short->long sequences). Observed kernel preemption path that favored large-context kernels causing micro-scheduling starvation for small-request lanes.

2026-03-10 03:30 UTC: Emergency mitigation applied: introduced an admission gate to limit concurrent warmup tasks per worker (queued warmup), temporarily increased small-request priority weight in router config, and disabled the new heuristic that allowed kernel preemption during warmup.

2026-03-11 09:00 UTC: Canary rollout to two Dedicated customers and one Hosted region. Canary telemetry shows TTFT p95 reduction from 420ms to 160ms and tokens/sec recovery to baseline for affected models.
2026-03-11 12:20 UTC: Customer-facing note prepared and sent by Support summarizing mitigation, ETA for full rollout, and workaround (pin to earlier model variant where available).
Risk: queued warmup introduces additional latency for cold-starts when queue depth is high; mitigated by exponential backoff for queued jobs and a fast-path for premium SLA customers.
Longer-term: follow-up tasks to optimize kernel-selection cost model, add per-tenant warmup budgets, and extend test harness to include mixed short/long fanout patterns in CI.
